# Lesson digest — one line per hard-won lesson (bible/06 §7)

Full text: `genesis-ctx lesson <ID>`. Areas: `genesis-ctx area <name>`.

- L-001 — ACP MCP env MUST be a list of `{name,value}`
- L-002 — `kiro_node` builds the real `KiroAgentOptions`
- L-003 — Keep the per-run SSE bus open until the run is TERMINAL; the client dedupes replayed history and CLOSES the EventSource on terminal final/error, else it reconnects and replays forever.
- L-004 — Data plane is SQLite, not JSON
- L-005 — Use only the canonical event kinds (run.started, node.completed, agent.*, validator.result, retry.scheduled, gate.*, run.final, error) — there is NO node.started/node.failed; running = run.cursor.
- L-006 — Workflows SHOULD declare a `graph:` topology whose node ids match LangGraph node names; without one, Run Detail derives a fallback from /steps so the graph is never blank.
- L-007 — The transcript folds `agent.*` events into turns (`buildTranscript` → `groupTurns`, validator/retry notes on the just-closed turn); Markdown answers reuse the existing renderers — no new deps.
- L-008 — A generic `worker_exit` must NOT clobber a specific `error` event; empty-message exceptions report their type + a hint.
- L-009 — LangGraph: sync `invoke` can't run async nodes and sync `SqliteSaver` fails under async (use `AsyncSqliteSaver`); `Command(resume=…)` needs a checkpointer-compiled graph.
- L-010 — ALL backend endpoints live under `/api`; the client prepends `/api` centrally and rejects non-JSON — uniform 500s on `/api/*` in the browser usually mean the backend isn't running.
- L-011 — Mirror the event/gate/topology/steps contract shapes in `web/src/types` + the golden fixtures; a contract drift must fail a test (stubs must not hide the contract).
- L-012 — MCP/CLI settings detail needs BOTH the merged card view and the custom entry, joined by name; the curated tier is read-only, the custom tier editable.
- L-013 — `workflow.yaml` may carry UI-only keys (e.g. `graph:` topology); the parity lint exempts them via `YAML_ONLY_KEYS`.
- L-014 — jest-axe v9 ships no types: keep its ambient `declare module` + matcher augmentation in the existing pure-ambient `.d.ts` files; extend the matcher globally in `web/src/test-setup.ts`.
- L-015 — Keep heavy web libs lazy (mermaid is dynamic-imported into its own chunk; Recharts is heavy too).
- L-016 — Credits are REAL, not estimated (Phase 11 / ADR-032).
- L-017 — Chat trust is fail-CLOSED — never trust-all; build allowlists in the namespaced `@server/tool` form; a curated server with no `tool_allowlist` is capped only by the node's `tools=` list.
- L-018 — sse-starlette frames SSE events with CRLF — a reader that splits only on LF-LF never parses a frame; accept both separators and don't let an LF-only test fixture hide it.
- L-019 — Secret writes must be atomic + serialized (v0.20.1 crash fix).
- L-020 — LangGraph's default `recursion_limit` is 25 supersteps — a looping workflow needs the worker to set a higher limit from META; `attach_reliability` keys retries by agent NODE NAME.
- L-021 — Never let a huge MCP result re-enter the context window: save it to the blackboard by reference (`save_tool_output`) and never paste tool output into the reply.
- L-022 — Workflow graph.py with custom reducer state keys must NOT use `from __future__ import annotations`.
- L-023 — Parse saved MCP tool outputs DEFENSIVELY — real shapes vary per tool (Phase 12 live-run lesson).
- L-024 — Kiro Skills load over ACP from the filesystem, NOT the wire (Phase 14 spike, 2026-07-16).
- L-025 — Pin the linter — unpinned `ruff` drifts and breaks CI on pre-existing code (Phase 16-02).
- L-026 — A blocking DB write inside an async node deadlocks the LangGraph checkpointer — do blocking `genesis.db` writes OFF the event loop (Phase 16-03).
- L-027 — Pin ruff in EVERY repo that runs `ruff check` in CI (16-08 recurrence of the 16-02 lesson).
- L-028 — MCP introspection must allow a large `tools/list` line (16-08).
- L-029 — Managed-native launch vs. env-resolution boundary (16-08, ADR-038).
- L-030 — The genesis `frontend` CI job runs only on `changes: [web/**/*]`; a follow-up tag touching no web file does NOT re-run the stale-bundle guard — force it with a real `web/**` touch.
- L-031 — Match the real Appian Deployment REST contract for the export — read the vendor's own client, don't guess (16-07 live fix).
- L-032 — De-dupe KB objects by UUID — real exports repeat UUIDs (16-07 live fix).
- L-033 — A newly-released library workflow must be `genesis install`-ed before it can run — and a missing workflow must not 500 (Phase 17-05 live).
- L-034 — Rendering a real graph needs level-of-detail, not `fitView`-to-fit (Phase 17-05 live).
- L-035 — Parser dependency extraction must scan EVERYTHING, and "orphan" ≠ "unbundled" (Phase 18).
- L-036 — An Appian prefixed id `_a-<base>_<suffix>` shares its base with folder-siblings — base is a GROUP id, not an object id (Phase 18).
- L-037 — APPREF/ENTRYPOINT is a by-name cross-app integration mechanism (Phase 18, user-taught).
- L-038 — When porting a parser front-half, you may silently drop whole layers — diff against the source (Phase 18).
- L-039 — A repository list method must populate the SAME derived fields its single-get promises (Phase 19 live fix).
- L-040 — Google-native export → converge on the binary parser; auto-sync on add (Phase 19).
- L-041 — An agent that must AUTHOR files needs BOTH cwd=sandbox AND the fs tool trusted — and know that fs writes vs tool permissions are separate gates (Phase 20, two live fixes).
- L-042 — Give a CLI agent bulk context as FILES in its workspace, not as chat content (Phase 20).
- L-043 — Embedding a 3rd-party browser SDK: prefer `postMessage`-host reuse over running its server (Phase 20, ADR-043).
- L-044 — The Kiro ACP extension surface is richer than the public docs — spike the *installed* CLI, and prefer typed methods over `execute` (Phase 21).
- L-045 — Exposing the CLI surface in a "read-only" chat = refine the ADR, keep the human-confirm backstop (Phase 21, ADR-045).
- L-046 — Route Kiro slash commands through the normal `prompt()` path, NOT `_kiro.dev/commands/execute` (v0.46.1 hotfix).
- L-047 — The chat MD export must match the REAL return shapes (v0.46.1 hotfix).
- L-048 — The built SPA must ship as PACKAGE DATA, and Dev-MCP enumeration must surface errors + paginate (v0.48.2).
- L-049 — A managed-MCP bundle can silently disagree with the registry on env-var names (v0.48.2 / genesis-workflows v0.9.4).
- L-050 — "delta" sync = full re-export + LOCAL diff, not an environment patch; and a scheduled Appian export must be serialized (Phase 23).
- L-051 — Shipping = clone + git-tag self-update, browser-based — reuse Friday's model, verify against the real CLI (Phase 22).
- L-052 — A launcher/process-control belongs in ONE place (Phase 22).
- L-053 — A workflow that reads a core Appian credential must resolve it via the ADR-048 env seam, not `ctx.secrets` (v0.9.6 live fix, app↔workflow version skew).
- L-054 — A managed-native CLI's `--output` may be confined to the process cwd — set `cwd`, pass a relative `-o` (gws 0.22.5, Phase 19 live fix).
- L-055 — Rendering a large parsed document to HTML on the main thread freezes the tab — show source for big docs (v0.50.2 live fix).
- L-056 — Verify the release commit contains EVERY changed file before tagging — a forgotten `git add` ships a test without its implementation and reds CI (v0.51.0 → v0.51.1).
- L-057 — When you bump a repo's tag, update EVERY transitive pin that must move with it — a downstream repo pinning an older shared dep reds CI with `ResolutionImpossible` (Phase 26 release, genesis-workflows v0.10.0).
- L-058 — An app-process run→artifact bridge (StageFinalizer, ChatRunSupervisor) can miss a live terminal event — give it a level-triggered recovery AND make its failures loud (Phase 29 v0.55.2).
- L-059 — A cursor jumping BACKWARDS in the live run graph is usually the bounded verify→revise loop, not corruption (Phase 29).
- L-060 — A completed run showed a mid-graph node stuck "Running" because the client `/events` fetch is capped and node status was event-derived (Phase 29 v0.56.0).
- L-061 — A run→artifact finalizer that sweeps "all done runs" must scope to the stage's CURRENTLY-BOUND run, and never restart `serve` while a run is active (Phase 29 v0.56.2).
- L-062 — Generalize a run→artifact finalizer with a workflow→stage BINDING REGISTRY, and gate `start` on the run lifecycle — not just "in progress" (Phase 30 / ADR-058).
- L-063 — A prerequisite (gated) stage is an amendment to the parallel model — enforce it on BOTH sides + expect it to pull into the roll-up (Phase 30).
- L-064 — A single agent turn that must emit a large multi-part artifact will hit `turn_timeout` and TRUNCATE — decompose + assemble deterministically (Phase 30 post-ship, genesis-workflows v0.14.0).
- L-065 — A gate→END terminal path must set a terminal status, or the worker's snapshot leaks the resumed 'running' (Phase 30 post-ship).
- L-066 — Never derive the run-graph's node status OR its full conversation from the whole event log on every tick — it's O(events²) and stalls large runs (Phase 30 post-ship perf).
- L-067 — Pre-reverse back-edges of a cyclic workflow graph before ELK layout and route edges around nodes — ELK/dagre's own cycle-breaking scatters the validators (Phase 30 run-graph revamp).
- L-068 — Serve the SPA `index.html` with `Cache-Control: no-cache` (Phase 30 post-ship).
- L-069 — `<Button asChild>` is broken in this codebase — never use it (Phase 31 live fix, v0.59.1).
- L-070 — A stale server-scoped `appian-dev/LCP_URL` secret silently overrides the env-derived dev URL → a 401 against the WRONG Appian environment (2026-09-06 live).
- L-071 — A permissive local Hub emulator hid a real contract mismatch — the first live `stage_artifact` publish 400'd (2026-09-06, genesis v0.66.2).
- L-072 — A read-only pull mirror must reconstruct local fields the frozen Hub contract doesn't carry — and the consuming UI must render a chat-less pulled artifact (2026-09-07, genesis v0.66.3–v0.66.5, collaboration puller).
- L-073 — A chat-authored artifact's `html_path` is NULL until a milestone — resolve stage HTML via the sandbox-aware `_current_stage_html`, not the raw column (2026-09-09, genesis v0.68.1).
- L-074 — Auto-derived board membership + an always-on pull loop + a wrong default-status = a board that "adds everything and won't behave" (2026-09-09, genesis v0.69.0).
- L-075 — A verify→revise loop that re-runs the WHOLE workflow (or can't touch frozen per-block content) is the single largest avoidable credit waste — add a second reliability tier that heals in place (Phase 40, ADR-067).
- L-076 — Don't fan a single deliverable out into per-item agent turns when the items must be mutually consistent — you lose cross-item context (story-design-analysis v0.3.0, ADR-062 amendment).
- L-077 — Never merge a PARTIAL parse through a whole-app merge — guard it in the store, not only in the caller (Phase 45, 45-01).
- L-078 — The live Appian side can differ from the documented contract — and from the local emulator — in ways only a live run shows (Phase 45-05/45-09).
- L-079 — Exported Appian XML can contain per-export random values — keep them out of change-detection hashes (Phase 45-09, F2).
- L-080 — A watermark must be captured BEFORE the work it covers, and must not come from someone else's snapshot (Phase 45-06/45-08).
- L-081 — A new default that turns a job ON, or a new stored home for a value, must respect user edits and old consumers — including an older client's explicit flag (Phase 45-07).
- L-082 — A pull must never re-apply a version this machine already holds — and one unresolvable record can pin a cursor for weeks (Phase 46-10 live finding).
- L-083 — Test fixtures must use the real value shapes — a stub label without "§" hid a doubled "§§" (Phase 46-07 review).
- L-084 — Appian `a!fromJson` silently turns date-looking strings into datetimes; the Hub returns null text as `""` (Phase 46-09 Hub build).
- L-085 — A client-side publish hook that nothing calls is invisible until a live two-machine check (Phase 46-10 F1, pre-existing since 38-04).
- L-086 — Program-owned IDs inside agent-authored HTML stay stable when the normalizer edits only start tags (Phase 46-02).
- L-087 — Migrate a large doc corpus by MOVING text with scripts and adding a sidecar index — never by having an agent read and rewrite it; probe the real CLI before designing against its docs (Phase 47).
- L-088 — Guard agent shells with a command-parsing PreToolUse hook, not prefix globs, and test every guard with a bypass corpus AND a positive corpus (Phase 47).
- L-089 — Never batch dependent steps or a verifying read with the step it proves: one per message, since a message's calls run in parallel; check a bundle commit with `git show --stat <sha> -- web/static` after the build has exited and settled (Phase 48).
- L-090 — Size table columns from a real-browser geometry probe at several widths, not percentages chosen by eye — jsdom computes no layout, so class-level tests only pin a fix (Phase 48).
- L-091 — With Python sqlite3's default transaction control, a transaction that SELECTs to validate and then writes is not atomic: take the write lock first (BEGIN IMMEDIATE or the CAS write), then validate (Phase 49).
- L-092 — pytest imports by module name: a tests/__init__.py in two workflow folders runs one's tests twice and the other's never; and never name a non-test module or symbol test* (Phase 49).
- L-093 — Store a terminal state before announcing the event that describes it, and test run→app bridges through the real RunManager._finalize: announce-then-store made every live finalizer a silent no-op (Phase 49).
- L-094 — Adding a registry value, hooking "every path that does X", or acting on a derived state reaches only what you grep: list every consumer, writer and producing path, backend and web, and opt out where needed (Phase 49).
- L-095 — Store an object UUID only when the local KB confirms it (a current kb_objects row); otherwise keep the link unresolved by name + type, since an unconfirmed UUID reads as removed (Phase 49).
- L-096 — Register a specific route before a generic path-param route that also matches it, and prove the order by behaviour: FastAPI 0.139+ wraps an included router in one _IncludedRouter entry (Phase 49).
- L-097 — A startup sweep that treats 'no worker tracked here' as orphaned must first hold an exclusive run-owner lock, or it fails a live peer server's runs; a recovery that writes a terminal state is not harmless (Phase 49).
- L-098 — With no internal dependency entries pip cannot see a missing or stale library: check presence in the CLI before its first internal import, and test each library's PEP 610 install origin (Phase 50).
- L-099 — Before unifying versions, move behaviour keyed on a version string to its own constant; an editable dev venv makes the bump live at commit time, not at release (Phase 50).
- L-100 — Never call glab api …/variables (or any CI-variables API) from an agent: it returns values in clear, masking only hides job logs; treat a value that reached agent output as leaked and rotate it (Phase 50).
- L-101 — In a non-TTY agent shell npx assumes --yes and installs whatever the registry serves under a name: run an internal tool as npx --no-install <bin> from its own install, never a bare npx <bin> (Phase 51).
- L-102 — A SQLite table rebuild needs the migration runner: PRAGMA foreign_keys is a no-op inside a transaction, so turn keys off before an explicit BEGIN and compare foreign_key_check rows on (table, rowid, parent) (Phase 51).
- L-103 — A derived index with no foreign key must not outlive its source: delete its rows in the same transaction as the source, and have every reader that counts them as live users join to the source (Phase 51).
- L-104 — To reap a run's processes, record each detached daemon's own pid and match on full command lines (/proc/<pid>/cmdline or ps -ww: procps cuts to COLUMNS), and log a tool failure before it reads as empty (Phase 51).
- L-105 — Scrub a whole Playwright report folder for secrets, zips decoded, in every escaped form (raw, JSON, XML): the HTML report keeps step titles such as Fill "<password>" that the JSON report drops (Phase 51).
- L-106 — A gate's prompt is a promise: when the route after an answer depends on the run's state, build the prompt from that state too, or the person's answer is silently overridden (Phase 51).
- L-107 — A background job or capture must reach a terminal state on every error path: mark it done in a finally, give a check added before a protected call the same protection, and keep cancel reaping late children (Phase 51).
- L-108 — Record an intended stop (pause, cancel) per worker before the kill and make the terminal write a compare-and-set, or the killed worker's exit fails the run or emits a second run.final (Phase 51).
- L-109 — Give a contract one home and one reader: show what the code declares instead of re-entering it in a form, and route every consumer through the same parser, proven by a parity test (Phase 51).
- L-110 — Prove code only by what ran: a unit counts only when its own step ran and passed, at the recorded base, over its whole dependency closure, from files nobody changed, never by an import or a lone replay (Phase 51).
- L-111 — Code review and gates do not replace live acceptance: budget a live pass on the real environment, and when a release goes first, say plainly everywhere that acceptance is still open (Phase 51).
- L-112 — Work kept local until the release first meets CI at the tag: give long local work one CI run, or one run in the CI image, before the release commit, and never let a test assume a tool that image lacks (Phase 51).
